units.title: Sounds, letters and the alphabet
goals: Read any Portuguese word aloud from its spelling, because the spelling-to-sound rules are regular
Know every letter, its name, and the sound or sounds it can represent
Tell oral vowels from nasal vowels and recognize diphthongs
Know how letter combinations and position change a sound ('c'/'ç'/'qu', 'g'/'gu'/'j', 's', 'x', 'r'/'rr', 'lh', 'nh', 'ch', 'h', final 'l', 't'/'d' before 'i', final 's')
grammar: The alphabet: 26 letters, their names, and the loan letters 'k', 'w', 'y'
The seven oral vowels and the five nasal vowels, with the tilde and the 'm'/'n' that nasalize
Diphthongs and triphthongs, and the 'ão'/'ães'/'õe' endings
Consonants with more than one sound and the spelling rules that choose between them ('c'/'ç'/'qu', 'g'/'gu'/'j', 's'/'ss'/'z', 'x', 'r'/'rr', 'h', 'lh'/'nh'/'ch')
Sounds that depend on position in Brazilian Portuguese: final 'l', final 's' and 'z', 't' and 'd' before 'i', unstressed final vowels
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each sound or spelling rule
letter names and spelling your own name aloud
minimal pairs that differ by one sound

units.title: Stress and the accent marks
goals: Know which syllable is stressed in a word without an accent mark
Know what each diacritic does: acute, circumflex, grave, tilde, cedilla
Explain why 'você', 'ônibus', 'avó', 'avô', 'café', 'português', 'está' and 'pôde' are written as they are
Read and write accents correctly, because they change pronunciation and sometimes meaning
grammar: Syllables and how to count them; the stressed syllable
The default stress rule by word ending, and why words that break it carry a written accent
The acute (open vowel or stress), the circumflex (closed vowel), the tilde (nasal), the grave (contraction only, crase) and the cedilla ('ç')
Accent marks that distinguish pairs: 'pode'/'pôde', 'por'/'pôr', 'para'/'pára' (old), 'avó'/'avô', 'é'/'e', 'está'/'esta'
Accents in plurals and verb forms, and the post-2009 spelling reform (no trema, no accent in a few diphthongs and hiatus)
vocabulary_themes: words that show each accent mark and each stress pattern
minimal pairs that differ only by an accent or by stress
the vocabulary already seen in the previous lesson, now written with its accents explained

units.title: How Portuguese works: the big picture
goals: See the structure of a Portuguese sentence and how it differs from English
Understand grammatical gender, number and agreement
Understand that verbs change for person and tense, and why subject pronouns are often dropped
Know the vocabulary of grammar used throughout this course: noun, article, adjective, verb, infinitive, conjugation, tense, mood, pronoun, preposition, contraction
grammar: Word order: subject, verb, object; adjectives usually after the noun; no 'do' support for questions or negation
Nouns have gender (masculine or feminine) and number; articles and adjectives agree with them
Verbs: the infinitive ('-ar', '-er', '-ir'), conjugation by person and number, and the three regular patterns
Subject pronouns, the dropped subject, and the system of address in Brazil ('você', 'a gente', 'tu', 'o senhor')
Prepositions and the contractions they form with articles ('de'+'o' = 'do', 'em'+'a' = 'na')
Questions and negation: intonation, question words, and 'não' before the verb
vocabulary_themes: the technical words for the parts of speech, in English and Portuguese
the very small set of function words used in every sentence ('o', 'a', 'de', 'em', 'que', 'e', 'não')

units.title: Greetings and introductions
goals: Greet people at different times of day
Introduce yourself and ask someone's name
grammar: Subject pronouns: 'eu', 'você', 'ele', 'ela', 'nós', 'a gente', 'vocês', 'eles', 'elas'
Present of 'ser' ('eu sou', 'você é', 'ele é', 'nós somos', 'eles são')
Fixed greeting formulas: 'tudo bem?', 'prazer', 'como vai?'

units.title: Ser, estar and how you feel
goals: Distinguish permanent from temporary states in simple cases
grammar: Full present of 'ser' and 'estar'
'Ser' vs 'estar': identity, origin, profession, characteristics vs location, temporary states, feelings
Adjective agreement in gender and number
Negation with 'não'

units.title: Numbers, time and dates
goals: Say your age and phone number
grammar: Cardinal numbers 0-100
'Ter' in the present and its use for age ('tenho 30 anos')
Telling time with 'É uma hora' vs 'São duas horas', 'meia', 'quinze', 'em ponto'
Days of the week (feminine '-feira'), months, ordinal 'primeiro' for the first of the month
vocabulary_themes: months and seasons of the calendar

units.title: Family, articles and possessives
goals: Use definite and indefinite articles correctly
grammar: Definite ('o', 'a', 'os', 'as') and indefinite ('um', 'uma', 'uns', 'umas') articles; noun gender
Regular plural formation including '-ão', '-l', '-m' endings
Possessives 'meu'/'minha'/'seu'/'sua'/'nosso'/'nossa' and 'dele'/'dela'/'deles'/'delas' for clarity
'Ter' in the present; 'de' for possession ('o carro da Ana')

units.title: Food, drinks and ordering
goals: Order in a restaurant, padaria and lanchonete
Say what you like and want
grammar: Regular present tense: '-ar' ('falar'), '-er' ('comer'), '-ir' ('partir'/'abrir')
'Querer', 'gostar de', 'preferir', 'eu queria' for polite requests, 'me vê' / 'quero' in service contexts
Questions with 'você quer/gosta de...?' and intonation questions
Partitive usage: 'um pouco de', 'mais', 'menos'
vocabulary_themes: Brazilian breakfast and everyday food ('pão na chapa', 'café com leite', 'pão de queijo', 'arroz e feijão')

units.title: Daily routine
goals: Use time expressions and frequency adverbs
Talk about work and study schedules
grammar: Reflexive verbs in the Brazilian pattern ('eu me levanto', 'ele se veste'), proclitic placement
Irregular presents: 'fazer', 'ir', 'sair', 'ver', 'dar', 'ler', 'pôr'
Frequency adverbs: 'sempre', 'geralmente', 'às vezes', 'nunca', 'todo dia'
Prepositions of time: 'às', 'de manhã'/'à tarde'/'à noite', 'de segunda a sexta', 'por volta de'

units.title: Places and directions
goals: Use 'ir' and 'estar' for movement and location
grammar: 'Ir' in the present; 'ir a'/'para'; 'estar em'
Prepositional contractions: 'de'+'o'='do', 'em'+'o'='no', 'a'+'o'='ao', 'por'+'o'='pelo' and with 'a'/'os'/'as'
Prepositions of place: 'perto de', 'longe de', 'ao lado de', 'em frente a', 'atrás de', 'entre', 'em cima de'
Imperative-like directions: 'vire', 'siga', 'atravesse', 'continue' ('você' form)

units.title: Shopping, colors and prices
grammar: Demonstratives 'este'/'esse'/'aquele' and 'isto'/'isso'/'aquilo' with the Brazilian everyday tendency to use 'esse'/'essa' for both near and mid distance
Numbers 100 to 1,000,000; reais and centavos
Adjective placement and agreement for colors
Questions: 'quanto custa'/'quanto é'/'quanto está', 'qual', 'quais'

units.title: Home and housing
goals: Say what exists in a place
Rent or ask about an apartment
grammar: Existential 'tem' (colloquial) and 'há' (formal): 'Tem um sofá na sala'
'Muito'/'pouco'/'bastante'/'tanto' as adjectives and adverbs
'Estar' + location, 'ficar' for location
Adjectives for describing places ('grande', 'pequeno', 'claro', 'barulhento')
vocabulary_themes: rooms and parts of the house

units.title: Plans, weather and leisure
goals: Talk about future plans with 'ir' + infinitive
Invite someone and accept or decline
grammar: Near future: 'ir' + infinitive ('eu vou viajar amanhã')
'Poder', 'querer', 'saber', 'precisar', 'dever' + infinitive
Weather expressions: 'está calor', 'faz frio', 'está chovendo', 'tem sol'
Invitations: 'Vamos...?', 'Que tal...?', 'Você topa?', declining politely

units.title: A1 consolidation
goals: Combine A1 skills in realistic conversations
Handle simple situations: cafe, shop, directions, small talk
grammar: Review: pronouns, 'ser'/'estar'/'ter'/'ir', present regular and irregular, articles, contractions, 'ir' + infinitive
Question formation review
Common beginner errors ('ser' vs 'estar', gender agreement, contractions, 'ter' vs 'haver')
Connecting sentences with 'e', 'mas', 'porque', 'então'
vocabulary_themes: survival phrases ('não entendi', 'fala mais devagar', 'como se diz...?')

units.title: The past: regular preterite
goals: Say what you did yesterday and last weekend
grammar: Pretérito perfeito of regular '-ar', '-er', '-ir' verbs, all persons with the Brazilian 'a gente' / 'eles' usage
Spelling changes: '-car'/'-çar'/'-gar' ('toquei', 'comecei', 'paguei')
Past time markers: 'ontem', 'anteontem', 'semana passada', 'há dois dias', 'faz um mês'
Past questions and negation
vocabulary_themes: weekend and daily activities in the past

units.title: The past: irregular preterite
goals: Use the most common irregular past forms
Narrate a short story in sequence
Talk about a trip or an event
grammar: 'ser'/'ir' ('fui', 'foi', 'fomos', 'foram'), 'ter', 'estar', 'fazer', 'dar', 'ver', 'vir', 'poder', 'querer', 'dizer', 'trazer', 'pôr', 'saber'
Stem-changing and vowel-change patterns in the preterite
Sequencing words: 'primeiro', 'depois', 'em seguida', 'então', 'por fim'
Contrast preterite vs present perfect meaning (Brazilian prefers the simple past)

units.title: The imperfect: habits and descriptions
goals: Talk about childhood and past habits
grammar: Pretérito imperfeito: regular forms and irregulars 'ser', 'ter', 'vir', 'pôr'
Uses: habits, descriptions, ongoing background, ages, time and weather in the past
'Costumar' + infinitive; 'sempre' with the imperfect
Imperfect progressive: 'estava' + gerund

units.title: Preterite versus imperfect
goals: Choose correctly between the two past tenses
Tell a story with background and events
Explain what was happening when something occurred
grammar: Event vs background: while an action was ongoing when another happened ('estava... quando...')
Verbs that change meaning ('saber', 'conhecer', 'querer', 'poder', 'ter') in the preterite vs imperfect
Narrative structure: setting, trigger, result
Time connectors: 'enquanto', 'quando', 'de repente', 'naquele dia'

units.title: Health and the body
goals: Describe symptoms at the doctor or pharmacy
grammar: 'Doer': 'dói' / 'doem' with indirect objects ('Dói a cabeça' / 'Me dói a cabeça'); 'estar com' + noun for symptoms
'Ter que'/'precisar'/'dever' + infinitive for advice
Affirmative and negative imperative forms for advice ('tome', 'não coma')
Reflexive and possessive with body parts ('lavar as mãos', 'meu braço')

units.title: Travel and transport
grammar: Preposition use with transport ('de ônibus', 'de avião', 'a pé', 'em casa') and destinations ('ir a'/'para'/'em')
'Querer'/'gostar de'/'precisar' in the conditional-polite 'eu queria'/'gostaria'
Time and schedule expressions: 'sai às', 'chega às', 'demora', 'a partir de'
Review of past tenses in trip narratives

units.title: Comparing things and people
goals: Say something is the best or the most
Give opinions about places and products
grammar: 'mais'/'menos' + adjective + ('do') 'que'; 'tão... quanto'; 'tanto'/'tantos... quanto'
Irregular comparatives: 'melhor', 'pior', 'maior', 'menor', 'mais velho'/'mais novo'
Superlatives: 'o mais'/'menos... de'; '-íssimo'
Prefer and 'mais ou menos', 'igual', 'parecido com', 'diferente de'

units.title: Instructions and the imperative
grammar: Imperative with 'você'/'vocês' (derived from the present subjunctive stem), affirmative and negative
Irregular imperatives: 'seja', 'vá', 'dê', 'saiba', 'esteja'
Imperative with reflexive and object pronouns in Brazilian speech ('me ajuda', 'me diz')
Impersonal instructions with infinitive ('Não fumar') and the use of 'dá pra' / 'pode'

units.title: Object pronouns
goals: Use 'me', 'te', 'lhe', 'o'/'a' and the colloquial alternatives naturally
grammar: Direct vs indirect objects; 'me', 'te', 'nos' as both; 'o'/'a'/'os'/'as'; 'lhe'/'lhes'
Brazilian colloquial pattern: 'ele'/'ela' as object, dropping 'o'/'a', 'vi ele', 'te amo', 'me liga'
Placement: before the verb in speech ('me disse'), after in formal writing ('disse-me') and with 'ir' + infinitive
Pronouns with prepositions: 'para mim', 'comigo', 'contigo', 'conosco'; the verb 'dar' + indirect pronoun

units.title: Work, jobs and the progressive
goals: Talk about your job and workplace
Handle simple phone calls and messages
grammar: Present progressive: 'estar' + gerund ('-ando', '-endo', '-indo') and irregular gerunds ('pondo', 'vindo', 'dizendo')
'Ficar': stay, become, be located, 'fiquei sabendo'
Present vs progressive: habit vs ongoing action
Time expressions: 'agora', 'neste momento', 'atualmente', 'ainda', 'já'
vocabulary_themes: office and phone phrases ('alô', 'quem fala?', 'vou transferir', 'um momento')

units.title: Future and polite requests
goals: Talk about the future in more than one way
grammar: Simple future of regular and the irregular verbs ('farei', 'direi', 'trarei') vs the colloquial 'ir' + infinitive
Conditional (futuro do pretérito) for politeness: 'gostaria', 'poderia', 'deveria', 'seria'
Suggestions and advice: 'Por que você não...?', 'Se eu fosse você...' (introduced as fixed phrases)
Probability with the future and 'deve ser'

units.title: A2 consolidation
goals: Tell a story using several past tenses
Write a short email or message
grammar: Review: preterite, imperfect, progressive, comparatives, imperative, object pronouns, future
Connectors: 'mas', 'porém', 'então', 'por isso', 'porque', 'quando', 'enquanto', 'embora' (intro)
Common A2 errors (pretérito vs imperfeito, pronoun placement, gender and number)
Writing short messages and emails with simple structure

units.title: Compound past and participles
goals: Use the Portuguese present perfect ('ter' + 'particípio') correctly
grammar: Pretérito perfeito composto: repeated or continuing action up to now ('tenho estudado'), unlike the English present perfect
Regular and irregular participles ('feito', 'dito', 'visto', 'aberto', 'escrito', 'posto', 'vindo'; 'ganho'/'ganhado', 'pago'/'pagado')
'Acabar de' + infinitive, 'ter' + participle with 'já'/'ainda'/'nunca'/'ultimamente'
Participles as adjectives with agreement ('cansado', 'aberta', 'escritos')

units.title: The present subjunctive
goals: Use it after verbs of desire, request and emotion
Use it after 'talvez', 'tomara' and similar expressions
grammar: Formation from the 'eu' form of the present ('falar' -> 'fale'; 'fazer' -> 'faça'), irregulars ('ser', 'estar', 'ir', 'ter', 'saber', 'querer', 'haver', 'dar')
Triggers: 'querer que', 'esperar que', 'pedir que', 'desejar que', 'tomara que', 'talvez'
Same-subject infinitive vs different-subject 'que' + subjunctive
Fixed expressions: 'Que Deus te abençoe', 'Que bom!', 'Bom proveito!'

units.title: Subjunctive: opinion, doubt and purpose
goals: Express doubt, opinion and necessity with the subjunctive
grammar: Impersonal expressions: 'é importante'/'necessário'/'possível'/'provável que', 'é bom'/'pena que'
Doubt vs certainty: 'duvidar que', 'não acho que' (subjunctive) vs 'acho que', 'tenho certeza que' (indicative)
Conjunctions: 'para que', 'caso', 'embora', 'a menos que', 'sem que', 'contanto que', 'antes que'
Negative and questioned opinion verbs

units.title: The future subjunctive
goals: Use the future subjunctive in time and condition clauses
Say 'when I arrive' and 'if you want'
Contrast with the infinitive and indicative
grammar: Formation from the third person plural of the preterite ('falar' -> 'falarem' -> 'falar', 'falares', 'falar', 'falarmos', 'falarem')
Irregular forms: 'for', 'fizer', 'tiver', 'estiver', 'vier', 'puder', 'quiser', 'disser', 'pôr' -> 'puser'
'Quando', 'assim que', 'depois que', 'logo que', 'enquanto', 'sempre que' + future subjunctive for future events
'Se' + future subjunctive for real conditions: 'Se você quiser, eu ajudo'

units.title: Imperfect subjunctive and hypotheticals
goals: Talk about unreal and hypothetical situations
Give advice with 'se eu fosse você'
grammar: Imperfect subjunctive formed from the third person plural of the preterite ('falasse', 'comesse', 'partisse'; 'fosse', 'tivesse', 'fizesse')
'Se' + imperfect subjunctive + conditional: 'Se eu tivesse tempo, viajaria mais'
'Pedir'/'querer' in the past + 'que' + imperfect subjunctive ('Eu queria que você viesse')
Wish expressions: 'Quem me dera', 'Tomara que', 'Quem dera'

units.title: Relative clauses and connectors
goals: Build longer sentences with relative pronouns
grammar: Relative pronouns: 'que', 'quem', 'onde', 'o que', 'o qual', 'cujo'/'cuja', 'com quem', 'em que', 'de que'
Prepositions before relatives ('a pessoa com quem falei', 'o lugar de que gosto') and the colloquial 'que eu gosto'
Connectors: 'porém', 'contudo', 'entretanto', 'no entanto', 'portanto', 'logo', 'apesar de', 'mesmo que', 'já que', 'visto que', 'uma vez que'
Conjunctions in the indicative vs subjunctive review
vocabulary_themes: description of people and places in more detail

units.title: Passive and impersonal constructions
goals: Use the pronoun 'se' as passive and impersonal marker
grammar: Passive with 'ser' + participle + 'por' ('O livro foi escrito por...')
Passive-reflexive 'se' ('Vende-se casa', 'Aluga-se apartamento') and impersonal 'se' ('Precisa-se de')
'Estar' + participle for results ('A porta está aberta')
Indeterminate subject with third person plural ('Falam que...') and 'a gente', 'você' in impersonal speech

units.title: The personal infinitive
goals: Recognize and use the inflected infinitive
Decide when it is needed or optional
Understand it in formal and literary texts
grammar: Formation: infinitive + '-es', '-mos', '-em' ('falares', 'falarmos', 'falarem')
Use when the infinitive's subject differs from the main clause ('É melhor vocês irem'; 'Para nós sairmos')
After prepositions: 'antes de', 'depois de', 'sem', 'para', 'por' ('Depois de chegarmos...')
Optional vs required; colloquial speech often uses the plain infinitive or the subjunctive

units.title: Work, bureaucracy and formal register
goals: Deal with documents and public services
Use formal and informal registers appropriately
grammar: Formal register: 'o senhor' / 'a senhora', 'Prezado(a)', 'Atenciosamente', 'Cordialmente'
Request formulas: 'Gostaria de solicitar', 'Poderia me informar', 'Venho por meio desta'
Formal vs informal verb choice and address ('tu'/'você'/'o senhor' and regional variation)
Reported requests and polite refusals

units.title: Opinions, news and debate
grammar: Opinion expressions: 'Na minha opinião', 'Eu acho que', 'Pra mim', 'Concordo'/'Discordo', 'Tenho a impressão de que'
Hedging and softening: 'de certa forma', 'até certo ponto', 'pelo menos'
Intro to reported speech: 'ele disse que', 'ela perguntou se', 'pediu para'
Review of subjunctive vs indicative in argument
vocabulary_themes: politics and society in neutral terms

units.title: Reported speech
grammar: Tense backshift: presente -> imperfeito, perfeito -> mais-que-perfeito, futuro -> condicional, imperative -> subjunctive
Reporting verbs: 'afirmar', 'declarar', 'sugerir', 'prometer', 'negar', 'avisar', 'pedir', 'mandar'
Indirect questions with 'se' and question words; pronoun and time-reference changes ('hoje' -> 'naquele dia', 'aqui' -> 'lá')
Colloquial pattern: 'ele falou que vem' (present kept) vs formal backshift

units.title: Pluperfect and other compound tenses
goals: Use the pluperfect to talk about earlier past actions
Express regret and unfulfilled past hypotheticals
grammar: Mais-que-perfeito composto ('tinha feito') and simple ('fizera', literary)
Future perfect ('terei feito') and conditional perfect ('teria feito')
Perfect subjunctive and pluperfect subjunctive: 'tenha feito', 'tivesse feito'; 'Se eu tivesse sabido, teria ido'
'Ter'/'haver' as auxiliary; formal vs colloquial frequency

units.title: Idioms, slang and regional speech
goals: Understand common Brazilian slang and idioms
grammar: Discourse markers: 'tipo', 'né', 'então', 'aí', 'pô', 'cara', 'mano', 'tá', 'pois é', 'sei lá', 'é isso'
Regional variation: carioca, paulista, mineiro, nordestino, gaúcho ('tu' vs 'você', 'mandioca'/'aipim'/'macaxeira', 'bergamota'/'mexerica'/'tangerina')
Idioms ('dar um jeito', 'ficar de olho', 'pagar o pato', 'estar nas nuvens', 'ficar de boa', 'dar bola', 'cair a ficha')
Register: 'gíria' vs 'vulgaridade' vs formal; informal contractions ('tá', 'pra', 'cê', 'num', 'tô', 'né', 'vamo')
vocabulary_themes: idioms with body parts and animals

units.title: Advanced pronouns and placement
goals: Control formal pronoun placement in writing
grammar: Enclisis, proclisis and mesoclisis ('disse-me', 'não me disse', 'dar-lhe-ei') rules and when each is triggered
Combined pronouns ('mo', 'to', 'lho', 'lha') in formal and literary Portuguese and their colloquial substitutes
Functions of 'se': reflexive, reciprocal, passive, impersonal, inherent ('arrepender-se'), emphasis
Pronouns with 'ir' + infinitive and with compound tenses

units.title: Reading literature and poetry
grammar: Literary tenses and word order: inversion, mesoclisis, simple pluperfect
Figures of speech: 'metáfora', 'comparação', 'ironia', 'personificação', 'hipérbole'
Reading strategies: context clues, word families, prefixes and suffixes
Diminutives and augmentatives ('-inho', '-zinho', '-ão', '-ona') with affective meaning
vocabulary_themes: Gonçalves Dias 'Canção do exílio' and other public-domain poems

units.title: Formal writing and registers
goals: Write structured essays and formal letters
grammar: Essay structure: 'introdução', 'desenvolvimento', 'conclusão', with connectors ('em primeiro lugar', 'ademais', 'por conseguinte', 'em suma')
Formal address and closing formulas; avoiding colloquial contractions
Nominalization and concise noun phrases
Punctuation, crase, and spelling after the orthographic agreement (hífen rules, trema removal)

units.title: Brazilian culture, regions and history
goals: Read and discuss texts about Brazil
Talk about regions, festivals and traditions
grammar: Reading comprehension strategies and extended texts
Historical narration: preterite, imperfect, pluperfect, passive
Expressing cause, consequence and chronology in written Portuguese
Numbers, dates and percentages in formal texts
vocabulary_themes: regions and states (Norte, Nordeste, Centro-Oeste, Sudeste, Sul)
festivals (Carnaval, Festa Junina, Círio de Nazaré, Parintins)

units.title: B2 capstone: argument and nuance
goals: Combine all tenses and moods fluently
grammar: Full review of indicative, subjunctive, conditional, personal infinitive and pronoun placement
Nuance: concessive and adversative structures ('por mais que', 'ainda que', 'mesmo assim', 'apesar disso')
Emphasis structures: 'foi... que', 'é que', 'quem... é', 'o que... é'
Review of common B2 errors and advanced idiomatic usage
